second_order: performing the Argentina-themed April Fools takeover
theme_note: These codes enact the room's separate April Fools practice: copying Argentina's look, writing in mock Spanish, translating ordinary formats and arguing about the CSS. The format varies from headlines and recipes to front-page pushes and moderator reconciliation; it is not canvas work.

second_order: choosing what and where to draw
theme_note: These codes propose, compare or revise canvas subjects and locations before or beyond execution: flags, slogans, figures, symbols, coordinates and later additions. What varies is the proposed object and whether it is national, comic or commemorative.

second_order: organizing pixel work through plans, templates, and Discord
theme_note: These codes make collective placement possible by teaching the cooldown, concentrating discussion, dividing jobs, circulating templates or scripts, and directing people among Reddit, PlaceBR and Discord. What varies is whether the device teaches, recruits, routes or standardizes work.

second_order: building, repairing, and maintaining the shared work
theme_note: These codes report or request hands-on pixel labour: starting, aligning, cleaning, correcting, finishing and keeping drawings intact. The work varies from the main flag to words, hearts, stars and the avocado, and from first construction to repetitive maintenance.

These codes attack, expand over, resist, patrol or rally against named threats and neighbours. The direction varies between outward raids, territorial enlargement and defense against the Blue Corner, 7-1, vandals and the Void.

second_order: bargaining and exchanging help with neighbours
theme_note: These codes answer outside groups and canvas neighbours with requests, conditions, concessions, refusals, peace terms, mutual defense or reciprocal repair. What varies is the counterparty and whether the exchange ends in help, a boundary, an apology or no settlement.

second_order: policing who may change the shared work
theme_note: These codes identify alleged vandals, defend accused repairers, demand approval, enforce templates and boundaries, or refuse changes that threaten allies and agreed projects. What varies is the rule being enforced and whether mistaken ownership, stale state or apology repairs the accusation.

second_order: pushing back on how the campaign was run and represented
theme_note: These codes resist flooding, disorder, unsafe code, automation, repetitive flag talk, unoriginal use of the mural and stereotyped national imagery. The objection varies between room saturation, organizing failures, tool safety, lost playfulness and what Brazil chose to depict.

second_order: joking, celebrating, and telling the canvas story
theme_note: These codes turn work into a public account by joking about what appeared, announcing outcomes, thanking contributors, claiming pixels, explaining battles, assigning credit and correcting the remembered story. The tone varies from ridicule and mourning to victory, pride and contested authorship.

second_order: saving and rebuilding the finished record
theme_note: These codes preserve or reconstruct the event through images, videos, archives, recolorings, missing-episode corrections, snapshots, torrents, scripts and a proposed complete timelapse. What varies is whether participants save an available artifact or repair an incomplete retrospective.

second_order: carrying r/place past the canvas and back into ordinary talk
theme_note: These codes mark return to ordinary programming, reuse r/place language inside later news talk, or call people toward another pixel canvas. The common practice is making the finished event usable after placement; what varies is memory, metaphor and renewed participation elsewhere.
